To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the instantaneous application (i.e. the Heaviside step function) of an electric current in a micro thermoelectrical cooler (TEC) leads to an increase of its performance (COP), and that the increase in performance is more evident when the heat generation in the micro TEC is considered.
the analytical solution of the hyperbolic thermal behaviour of a thermoelectric cooler with instantaneous electric current is obtained and the COP of the device is increased by the hyperbolic model.
the analytical solution for the instantaneous electric current application in micro thermoelectric devices under the hyperbola model is derived for the first time.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the analysis of the transient heat conduction in micro thermoelectric cooling devices, which are used in a wide range of applications, including microelectronic devices, microelectromechanical systems, and microsensors.
the analysis of the ultrafast transient thermal behaviour of a thermoelectric device, in particular a thermoelectric cooler, under a hyperbolic heat transport model.
the study of the ultrafast thermal behaviour and performance of micro thermoelecric coolers under hyperbolic heat transport.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a hyperbolic analysis of the thermoelectric cooling process is a necessary step forward to understand and improve the thermal behaviour of the micro thermoelectric devices.
the parabolic model is a good approximation of the real physical behaviour of the device only when the heat generation is time independent.
the hyperbolic model is more suitable for the ultrafast transient analysis of the micro thermoelectric devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hyperbolic model is able to capture the ultrafast behaviour of the device and to predict the thermal behaviour at early times.
the hyperbolic model is able to capture the thermal behaviour of the micro cooler at early times, when the temperature wave front is present.
the analytical solution for the unsteady thermal behaviour in a micro thermoeletric cooler with the instantaneous application of electric current is presented for the first time in the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the instantaneous application and the sudden variation of electric current in thermoelectric coolings can be modelled in a simple way.
the hyperbolic model is a powerful tool in the analysis of ultrafast thermoelectric cool devices.
the parabolic heat conduction model does not represent the actual behaviour of a micro-TEC at very short times.
